summary: After damning report into standards at the top of forces in England and Wales, 200 people a year with superintendent potential to be recruitedHundreds of people will be trained to boost “frankly inadequate” leadership of law enforcement, the home secretary is to say.Shabana Mahmood will tell police chiefs and leaders at their central London annual conference on Wednesday that standards must improve as she unveils a scheme to train 200 people a year, after a report in June into police leadership found it was at times “staggeringly” poor.

stories.title: UK will miss climate targets if it weakens EV sales rules, advisers warn
summary: Analysts say mooted move to let more petrol and diesel vehicles be sold would wreck plan to reach net zero by 2050Weakening the UK’s electric car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss legally binding climate targets, according to advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero.The analysis by the Climate Change Committee (CCC) suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.

stories.title: Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat
summary: England’s exam regulator says those caught using AI or smart glasses face disqualification from GCSEs and A-levelsStudents in England could suffer “life-altering” penalties if they are caught relying on AI or smart glasses to cheat, England’s qualifications regulator has said.The head of Ofqual, Ian Bauckham, said students could be disqualified from GCSEs, A-levels and other qualifications if they tried to use AI in assessed coursework, and called for retailers to be barred from marketing wearable technology for exam cheating.
